questions.q: Where does a normally deleted record go (not a permanent delete)?
options: It's gone immediately with no way to recover it
The Recycle Bin, where it can be restored within a retention window
An automatic export file emailed to the org admin
A separate "Deleted Records" report only, not a recoverable location
questions.explain: A normal delete sends the record to the Recycle Bin, where it remains recoverable until the retention window expires or it's purged.

questions.q: What's the difference between My Recycle Bin and Org Recycle Bin?
options: My Recycle Bin shows records you deleted; Org Recycle Bin shows everything deleted org-wide
They are identical views with different names
Org Recycle Bin only shows records deleted by Mass Delete, never individual deletes
My Recycle Bin is available only to System Administrators
questions.explain: My Recycle Bin is scoped to your own deletions. Org Recycle Bin, visible to admins and permitted users, shows everything deleted across the org.

questions.q: What happens when you click Delete (not Restore) on a record already in the Recycle Bin?
options: It moves the record to a second-level recycle bin for another 15 days
It permanently removes the record immediately, with no further recovery possible
It restores the record automatically as a side effect
It only hides the record from view without actually removing it
questions.explain: Clicking Delete on a Recycle Bin record permanently removes it right away — the same irreversible outcome as a permanent mass delete.

questions.q: How long do records typically remain in the Recycle Bin before being purged?
options: 24 hours
15 days, or sooner if deleted-data storage fills up
90 days, with no exceptions
Indefinitely, until manually emptied
questions.explain: Records sit in the Recycle Bin for 15 days before automatic purging, though they can be purged earlier if an org's deleted-data storage limit is reached.

questions.q: A record was deleted 18 days ago and is needed back. Why won't the Recycle Bin help, and what's the realistic fallback?
options: The Recycle Bin would still have it; no fallback is needed
It's past the 15-day retention window, so the fallback is restoring from a data export or scheduled backup, if one exists from before the deletion
Mass Transfer Records can retrieve deleted records regardless of age
There is no possible recovery after any deletion, regardless of timing
questions.explain: 18 days exceeds the Recycle Bin's roughly 15-day window, so the record has likely been purged. The fallback is a data export or scheduled backup taken before the deletion — exactly why those exist as a second layer.
